'''Achille Sannia''' (14 April 1822 – 2 August 1892) was an Italian [[mathematician]] and [[politician]].

==Biography==

Achille Sannia was a senator of the [[Kingdom of Italy]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://notes9.senato.it/Web/senregno.NSF/e56bbbe8d7e9c734c125703d002f2a0c/cb3dd5403678a7054125646f00604f7d?OpenDocument|title=Scheda senatore SANNIA Achille|website=notes9.senato.it|access-date=2019-01-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304081818/http://notes9.senato.it/Web/senregno.NSF/e56bbbe8d7e9c734c125703d002f2a0c/cb3dd5403678a7054125646f00604f7d?OpenDocument|archive-date=2016-03-04|url-status=live|df=}}</ref>  He was born in [[Campobasso]] and later moved from [[Molise]] to [[Naples]] to continue his studies together with [[Enrico D'Ovidio]]. 
He first taught in a private school before moving to a University in 1865 as a professor of geometry.<ref name=unito/>

In 1871, he created a school of [[electrical engineering]]. He wrote two important treatises, one concerning [[projective geometry]] and the other [[elementary geometry]]. He was a member of the [[Academy of sciences|Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=unito>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dm.unito.it/sism/m_italiani/biografie/tricomi/sannia.html|title=Achille SANNIA|last=|first=|date=|website=www.dm.unito.it|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120229053213/http://www.dm.unito.it/sism/m_italiani/biografie/tricomi/sannia.html|archive-date=29 February 2012|url-status=|access-date=19 January 2019}}</ref>

He had a son, [[Gustavo Sannia]], who was also a mathematician.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://matematica.unibocconi.it/autore/gustavo-sannia|title=Gustavo Sannia {{!}} MATEpristem|website=matematica.unibocconi.it|access-date=2019-01-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151019085147/http://matematica.unibocconi.it/autore/gustavo-sannia|archive-date=2015-10-19|url-status=live|df=}}</ref>

==Works==

*[[Planimetrics|Planimetry]], with Enrico D'Ovidio, Stab. typ. of the fine arts, Naples 1869, II ed. 1871
*Geometry elements, with Enrico D'Ovidio, (14 editions), Naples 1868-69, 12th edition, B. Pellerano LC Scientific and Industrial Library successor, Naples 1906
*Projection Geometry Lessons dictated in the [[Royal University of Naples]] by Prof. Achille Sannia- Ed. Pellerano Naples 1891 of 691pagg.
